# LLM Prefill & Decode Speed Visualizer

An interactive tool for understanding LLM inference performance: prefill (compute-bound prompt ingestion, sets TTFT) vs decode (bandwidth-bound token generation, sets TPOT), across single-turn chat and multi-turn agentic loops.

<!-- agent-parseable:meta -->
Base-URL: https://llm-prefill-decode-visualizer.vercel.app
OpenAPI-Spec: /api/spec
Agent-Manifest: /agents.json
Endpoint-Index: /api/agent/index.json
Tabs: single,agentic,batching,compare,ab,diff,shortlist,kvcache,theory
Tab-URL-Template: {Base-URL}/?tab={id}
Tab-Section-Header-Format: ### Tab: {id} — {label}
Repo: https://github.com/riceharvest/llm-prefill-decode-visualizer
<!-- /agent-parseable:meta -->

## When to use this tool

Use this site (or its API) when you need to:

- **Choose hardware for running an LLM locally.** Compare measured tok/s across consumer GPUs, Apple Silicon and cloud endpoints before buying — e.g. "will a 3060 12GB run Qwen 72B at 32k context?" → `/api/vram?hfId=Qwen/Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct&context=32768&vramGb=12`.
- **Predict latency for a workload shape.** Given a prompt size and output length, get exact TTFT and TPOT for a hardware profile → `/api/compute?model=singleTurn&...`.
- **Reason about agentic loop costs.** Multi-turn tool-calling loops re-ingest history every turn; model the walltime growth with and without prefix caching → `/api/compute?model=agentic&...`.
- **Decide between quantizations or engine flags.** Compare KV-cache VRAM at INT4 vs FP8, or the documented delta of `--flash-attn` etc. → `/api/compute?model=kvCache&...` and `/api/compute?model=flagged&flags=flash-attn,kv-q8&...`.
- **Budget $ per million tokens** on owned hardware including electricity and amortization → `/api/compute?model=cost&...`.

Do NOT use this tool for: hosted-API pricing comparisons (it models owned
hardware only), training-time estimates, or non-transformer architectures.

## For AI agents — read this first

Everything on the page is available as plain JSON over HTTP. No browser needed.

Base URL: https://llm-prefill-decode-visualizer.vercel.app
OpenAPI spec: /api/spec (machine-readable, derive all endpoints from it)

### URL versioning (/v1/)

Every endpoint below is also served under a versioned prefix: replace `/api/` with `/v1/` (e.g. `/v1/compute?model=singleTurn&…`, `/v1/benchmarks`, `/v1/spec`). The two prefixes are identical — same handlers, same responses, same rate limits.

- **External consumers should harden onto `/v1/`.** It gives us room to ship breaking changes under a new prefix without silently breaking your integration.
- The unversioned `/api/*` paths keep working and remain where the docs live (`/api/spec`).
- Policy: additive changes never break existing clients; breaking changes ship under a new version prefix and the previous one is kept for at least 90 days with `Deprecation`/`Sunset` headers (see CHANGELOG-API.md in the repo for the full schema-versioning policy).

**GET /api/health** — liveness + upstream data freshness ({ok, upstreamFreshness, cacheAge}). Human status page at /status.html.

**GET /api/agent/freshness.json** — agent-readable data-freshness and confidence report (alias: /api/agent/confidence.json, same handler). Answers "how old are these numbers and how much should I trust them?" without fetching raw runs: upstream cache state, dataset-wide staleness (`fresh <90d | aging <1y | stale ≥1y`, `unknown` = no parseable date), per-group freshness + the same 0-100 confidence score used by /api/benchmarks and /api/best (sample size, IQR spread, outlier density; grades `high >=70 | medium >=40 | low <40`), major engine-release boundary warnings. Filters mirror the other data endpoints: `?hardware=` (substring), `?model=` (substring), `?quant=` (exact), `?context_band=`, `?max_age=<days>`, `?groupBy=hardware|model|hardwareModel`, `?snapshot=<id>`. Response: `{ description, endpoint, generatedAt, filters, cache, dataset, groups[], summary, caveats, relatedEndpoints }`. Identical computations to /api/benchmarks, /api/best and /api/health — this endpoint only wraps them.

### Endpoints

**GET /api/compute?model=<name>&<params>** — run any simulator math and get exact numbers.

Models:
- `singleTurn` — TTFT, TPOT, total walltime for a chat request. Params: `promptTokens`, `outputTokens`, `prefillSpeed`, `decodeSpeed`.
  Example: `/api/compute?model=singleTurn&promptTokens=4096&outputTokens=512&prefillSpeed=3800&decodeSpeed=105`
- `speculative` — effective decode speed with a draft model. Params: `baseDecodeSpeed`, `draftTokens`, `acceptanceRate`, `draftCostFraction`.
- `batched` — per-user vs aggregate throughput at batch size B. Params: `prefillSpeed`, `decodeSpeed`, `batchSize`, `promptTokens`, `outputTokens`, `decodeDecayExponent` (default 0.25, valid range 0–1: heuristic contention exponent — 0 = perfect linear scaling, 1 = batching gains nothing).
  ⚠️ **No saturation point:** aggregate throughput = `decodeSpeed × batchSize^(1 − decodeDecayExponent)` grows monotonically forever by construction (defaults: ×B^0.75). This model has NO knee, plateau, or "optimal batch size" — do not use it alone for sizing decisions (real schedulers saturate earlier via admission control and memory limits). To find where scaling stops paying off, sweep batch sizes and compare marginal gain per slot (see the homogeneous-sweep idiom under POST /api/compute).
- `agentic` — turn-by-turn walltime for a tool-calling loop, with/without prefix caching savings. Params: `numTurns`, `basePromptTokens`, `toolOutputTokensPerTurn`, `decodeTokensPerTurn`, `prefillSpeed`, `decodeSpeed`, `enablePrefixCaching`.
- `kvCache` — KV-cache VRAM for an architecture. Params: `architecture` (`llama70b|llama8b|qwen72b|mistral7b`) or explicit `numLayers`+`kvHeads`+`headDim`, plus `contextLength`, `precisionBytes` (2=FP16, 1=FP8, 0.5=INT4), `batchSize`. Units: `kbPerToken` is KiB, `totalMb` is MiB, `totalGb` is GiB — all binary (÷1024ⁿ), not decimal; the response declares this in its `units` block (#738 #866).
- `flagged` — engine launch-flag modeling. Params: `prefillSpeed`, `decodeSpeed`, `promptTokens`, `outputTokens`, and `flags` (comma-separated ids: `flash-attn,kv-q8,kv-q4,no-mmap,vllm-fp8-kv,vllm-o3`). Returns adjusted speeds, a per-flag audit trail (delta + source note), warnings, and a `singleTurn` simulation at the adjusted speeds. Deltas are documented heuristics, not measurements.
- `cost` — $/1M tokens for owned hardware: amortized purchase price + electricity over the measured speeds of a scenario shape. Params: `hardwarePriceUsd`, `electricityRatePerKwh` (default 0.15), `powerDrawWatts`, `amortizationMonths` (default 36), plus the usual `promptTokens`, `outputTokens`, `prefillSpeed`, `decodeSpeed`.
  Example: `/api/compute?model=cost&hardwarePriceUsd=2000&powerDrawWatts=450&electricityRatePerKwh=0.15&prefillSpeed=3800&decodeSpeed=105`

**GET /api/vram** — combined model + KV-cache + context VRAM from just an `hfId`. Architecture (layers, hidden dim, GQA heads, head dim) and weight size are resolved from the Hugging Face config automatically — you never look up model internals.
- `/api/vram?hfId=meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct&context=65536&quant=q4_k_m` → weights GiB + KV GiB + total, with the resolved architecture and the KV bytes/token formula. Every memory figure on this endpoint (weights, kvCache, total, fits.headroomGb) is **GiB — binary, 1024-based, NOT decimal GB**; the response declares this in its top-level `units` block (#738 #866). Pass budgets (`vramGb`) as GiB too.
- Add `&vramGb=24` → `fits` flag plus `maxContextTokens` that fit the budget (upper bound; ignores activation overhead).
- Add `&numTurns=40&tokensPerTurn=1200` → per-turn KV-growth projection with the exact turn where the context window (`firstContextOverflowTurn`) or VRAM budget (`firstVramOverflowTurn`) is first exceeded.
- `quant` accepts GGUF/GPTQ tags (fp16, fp8, q8_0, q6_k, q5_k_m, q4_k_m, q4_0, q3_k_m, q2_k…); unknown tags assume ~4-bit and set `inputs.quantAssumed: true`.
- GGUF-only repos (no safetensors metadata) fall back to the largest `.gguf` file size for weight VRAM.
- Resolution is three-tier (check `model.resolutionSource`): `builtin-table` — common families (llama*, qwen3*, gemma*, mistral*) resolve offline from a built-in config table, no huggingface.co call; `huggingface` — everything else resolves from the repo's config.json / GGUF header; `name-heuristic` — when HF is unreachable or gated but the model name carries a size tag ("Foo-13B"), a coarse bucketed estimate is returned with the assumption spelled out in `model.notes`. Bad ids still 404.

Calling `/api/compute` with no `model` returns a self-describing capability list.

**Batching (one round trip for N comparisons):** `POST /api/compute` with `{"batch": [{"model": "singleTurn", "promptTokens": 4096}, {"model": "kvCache", "architecture": "llama70b", "contextLength": 131072}]}` (also accepted as `variants`, or `?batch=[...]` as URL-encoded JSON on GET). Each item is a normal parameter set including its own `model` field; max 50 items. Response: `{batch: true, count, okCount, errorCount, results: [{index, ok, result | error}]}` — one bad scenario returns a per-item error instead of failing the whole batch.

**Homogeneous-sweep idiom (read a throughput curve in one call):** all 50 batch items may share the same `model` while you vary a single parameter — that turns one POST into a full parameter-response curve. Worked example, a batch-size curve for `model=batched` (B = 1..48; note a sweep this size uses 48 of the 50-item budget, and each POST counts as ONE request against the 120 req/min rate limit regardless of item count):

```bash
curl -s -X POST "$BASE/api/compute" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"batch":[{"model":"batched","decodeSpeed":105,"batchSize":1},{"model":"batched","decodeSpeed":105,"batchSize":2}, ...]}'
# → ordered results[i].result.aggregateDecodeTokPerSec points along the B axis
```

Results come back in request order with no axis metadata (`paramSwept` etc.), so track which value each index corresponds to client-side. To find where scaling stops paying off, compute the marginal gain between consecutive points (`aggregate(B+1) − aggregate(B)`); for `batched` it shrinks as ~B^−0.25 but never reaches zero — see the no-saturation caveat on the `batched` model above.

**Dry-run / sandbox (`dry_run=true`):** add `&dry_run=true` to any `/api/compute` call (or `"dry_run": true` in the POST body; also applies per-item inside a batch) to validate the request and echo the parsed parameters — defaults filled in, numbers coerced — WITHOUT executing any math. Response: `{dry_run: true, model, inputs, id?, note}`. The `id` is the same deterministic hash the real call would return, and failures (unknown model, malformed batch) behave exactly as they would for a real call — use it as a cheap sanity check before spending a real computation. Example: `/api/compute?model=agentic&numTurns=6&enablePrefixCaching=true&dry_run=true`.

Every `/api/compute` and `/api/best` response carries a deterministic `id` (`calc_<12 hex chars>`) hashed from the resolved request. Cite it to reference a result across turns:

**GET /api/calc/<id>?<original params>** — replay any computation from its id. Ids are pure content hashes, not database keys: resend the original parameters and the endpoint re-runs identical math and stamps `verified: true`. Example:
- `/api/compute?model=singleTurn&promptTokens=4096` → `{ "id": "calc_x", ... }`
- `/api/calc/calc_x?model=singleTurn&promptTokens=4096` → same numbers, `verified: true`
- For `/api/best` results add `endpoint=best`: `/api/calc/calc_y?endpoint=best&by=decode&maxParamsB=8`
- Altered parameters are rejected with `expected` = the id they actually hash to.

**GET /api/presets** — built-in hardware speed presets (RTX 4090, dual 3090, M3 Ultra, Groq, H100, RPi5…) and workload scenarios (RAG query, code generation…). Use these as `/api/compute` inputs.

**GET /api/localmaxxing** — community-measured single-stream benchmark runs (3,600+).
- No params: hardware-group summary (71 rigs, run counts).
- `?hardware=rtx 3090&limit=50`: runs for rigs matching that substring.
- `?model=qwen3.6-27b&limit=20`: runs for a model. `model` matches the **normalized family** — repo/quant/finetune variants collapse (`unsloth/Qwen3.6-27B-MTP-GGUF` and `mlx-community/Qwen3.6-27B-4bit` are both `qwen3.6-27b`).
- `?quant=q4_k_m`: exact quantization filter.
- Filtered calls are cursor-paginated: `{ total, items[], has_more, next_cursor }`, sorted by decode speed desc (runId tiebreak). Page size: `limit` (default 50, max 500). Follow `next_cursor` until `has_more` is false; cursors stay stable even when new runs land mid-scan.

**POST /api/localmaxxing** — submit a community benchmark run for review. JSON body with required `model`, `quant`, `hardware`, `hwClass` (`discrete_gpu|unified|cpu_only`), `prefillTokPerSec`, `decodeTokPerSec`; optional `engine`, token counts, `provenance` (`engineVersion`, `command`, `sourceUrl`, `notes`) and `submitter`. Server-side validation enforces sanity bounds per hardware class (a claimed 99,999 tok/s on an RPi5 is rejected) and rejects near-duplicates of existing runs (same model family + quant + rig within 10%). Valid submissions return `202` with a `submissionId` and are queued for manual review — they never publish immediately. Validation failures return `400` with machine-readable errors: `{"error":"validation_failed","errors":[{"field","code","message"}]}`.

**GET /api/runs** — one-shot machine-readable dump of the **full** run index: every community-measured run (comparable AND batched/non-comparable) as JSON or CSV — no pagination round-trips needed.
- `/api/runs?format=json` (default): `{ schemaVersion, generatedAt, rowCount, totalRunCount, comparableCount, comparableFilter, dataDictionary[], runs[] }`. Each run carries a `comparable` boolean so you can reproduce the single-stream filter client-side; `totalRunCount` tells you how much a subset left out and `comparableCount` how many rows the aggregate endpoints use.
- `/api/runs?format=csv`: RFC 4180 with a `#`-comment preamble carrying metadata + a data dictionary (skip `#` lines for clean tabular data); served as a dated attachment.
- Subset server-side with `?comparable=true|false|all` (default `all`). Shares the 10-minute cache with the other benchmark endpoints.

**Watch feeds (#109)** — subscribe to a hardware+model combo ("RTX 4090 + Qwen3 32B") and get notified when new community runs land for that pair.
- **RSS (no registration):** poll `/api/watch/rss.xml?model=Qwen3+32B&hardware=RTX+4090&quant=q4_k_m` in any feed reader. Filters mirror GET /api/localmaxxing (`days=N` bounds item age, default 30); newest matching runs first, max 50 items.
- **Register a watch:** `POST /api/watch {"model":"Qwen3 32B","hardware":"RTX 4090","quant":"q4_k_m","webhookUrl":"https://…"}` → `201 {watchId, secret, rssUrl, matchingExistingRuns}`. At least one of model/hardware is required; webhookUrl must be https and is optional (RSS works without it). The secret is shown once: it authorizes DELETE and is sent to your webhook as `X-Watch-Secret`.
- **Webhook delivery:** POST or GET `/api/watch/dispatch` (cron-friendly) delivers each webhook watch's unseen matching runs as a `watch.new_runs` JSON payload; per-watch results report delivery status. Set the `WATCH_DISPATCH_SECRET` env var to lock the endpoint down.
- **Manage:** GET /api/watch lists registered combos (no secrets); DELETE `/api/watch?id=<watchId>&secret=<secret>` unsubscribes.

**GET /api/benchmarks** — aggregated stats: median + IQR per group (outlier-resistant). Default groups by hardware×model-family; regroup with `?groupBy=hardware|model|quant`. Each group carries median/q1/q3/min/max for prefill and decode plus the single best measured run. Cursor-paginated like /api/localmaxxing: `{ total, items[], has_more, next_cursor }`, sorted by median decode desc (group key tiebreak); page size `limit` (default 25, max 200).

**GET /api/agent/benchmarks.json** — agent-friendly wrapper around the raw run search (same data as `search_runs` / GET /api/localmaxxing): one flat record per measured run with `runId`, `model`, `hardware`, `quantization`, `engine`, `prefillTokPerSec`, `decodeTokPerSec` (tok/s), `measuredAt`, `ageDays` and a `staleness` tier (`fresh <90d | aging <1y | stale ≥1y`). Filters mirror search_runs (`?hardware=` substring, `?model=` substring, `?quant=` exact, plus `?context_band=`, `?max_age=`, `?limit=` default 25 max 200, `?cursor=`, `?snapshot=`). Sorted fastest decode first; response carries `{ description, snapshot, filters, total, count, runs[], has_more, next_cursor, caveats, relatedEndpoints }`.

**GET /api/diff?runA=<id>&runB=<id>** — diff two measured runs in one call: both runs' metrics plus per-metric deltas, ratios (B ÷ A) and a plain-language summary. Time metrics are normalized to a 2048-token prompt / 512-token output.

**GET /api/diff?mode=whatif&a=<constraints>&b=<constraints>** — what-if decision diffing: pass two /api/best-style constraint sets and get back only the deltas — options entering/leaving the feasible set (`entered` / `left`, with rank positions) and per-option VRAM headroom change (`headroom`, from the estimated fit math; enable `fitCheck`/`contextLength` in the sets). Constraint sets accept JSON (`?a={"fitCheck":"true","contextLength":8192}`) or URL-encoded query strings (`?a=fitCheck=true&contextLength=8192`), or a POST body `{"mode":"whatif","a":{...},"b":{...}}`. Example: `/api/diff?mode=whatif&a=fitCheck=true&contextLength=8192&model=qwen&b=fitCheck=true&contextLength=65536&model=qwen` shows which rigs survive a 64k-context requirement and how much headroom the survivors lose.

**GET /api/best** — ranked answers to natural questions:
- `/api/best?by=decode&maxParamsB=8&quant=q4_k_m` → top rigs for ≤8B models at Q4_K_M
- `/api/best?by=prefill&hwClass=unified` → fastest prefill on unified-memory systems
- `/api/best?model=qwen3.6-27b` → fastest rigs for that model family
- `/api/best?model=qwen3.6-27b&fitCheck=true&contextLength=65536` → fastest rigs whose VRAM can actually hold it at 64k context (estimated: weights from params × quant bits + KV cache + 10% overhead)

**GET /api/sizing** — one-call deployment recommendation for agents. Pass a workload spec, get ranked hardware with the math attached:
- `/api/sizing?model=qwen&contextLength=32768&concurrency=4&maxTtftSeconds=2&maxTpotMs=50&maxVramGb=48`
- Each recommendation carries `vramFit` (weights from params × bits-per-weight + KV cache at target context × concurrency + overhead vs available VRAM/unified memory), `expected` TTFT/TPOT from aggregated benchmark medians with IQR, `confidence` from sample count, and `meetsSlo` flags. Ranked meet-SLO-first, then by median per-user decode. All memory figures — `maxVramGb` budget, `memoryGb` and every `vramFit` field — are **GiB (binary, 1024-based)**, not decimal GB; the response declares this in its top-level `units` block (#738 #866).
- `/api/best?by=cost&price=2000&electricityRate=0.15` → best tok/s-per-dollar. Ranks by **$/1M tokens** (lower is better): rig price amortized over `amortizationMonths` (default 36) + electricity at `electricityRate` $/kWh (default 0.15) and a per-hwClass power estimate (override with `powerWatts`), divided by effective throughput at median speeds for the scenario shape (`promptTokens`/`outputTokens`, default 2048/512). Each result carries its `costInputs` echo so you can see exactly what was assumed.

**GET /api/parse-constraints** — turn plain-language constraints into the canonical struct: `/api/parse-constraints?q=self-hosted%20Qwen%2027B%20at%20Q4%20for%2010%20users%20under%20%241500` → `{input, constraints, ambiguities, sizingQuery}`. Deterministic regex/heuristics (no LLM). `constraints` mirrors /api/sizing params with null for anything not stated; `ambiguities` lists every assumption ("10 users: assume 1 stream each or batched?") — resolve these before trusting downstream numbers; `sizingQuery` is a ready-made /api/sizing query string.

## Endpoint reference

Canonical curl + response shape for each core endpoint. All work identically under `/v1/` (e.g. `/v1/compute`); every response carries `schema_version` and rate-limit headers.

```bash
# Inference math for one request shape (TTFT, TPOT, walltime)
curl -s "$BASE/api/compute?model=singleTurn&promptTokens=4096&outputTokens=512&prefillSpeed=3800&decodeSpeed=105"
```
→ `{ id, inputs, warnings[], ttftSeconds, tpotMs, decodeSeconds, totalWalltimeSeconds, effectiveThroughputTokPerSec, prefillSharePct, decodeSharePct }` — e.g. ttftSeconds 1.077895, totalWalltimeSeconds 5.954085.

```bash
# Built-in hardware speed presets + workload scenarios
curl -s "$BASE/api/presets"
```
→ `{ description, hardware[{id, name, prefillSpeedTokPerSec, decodeSpeedTokPerSec, vramBandwidth, badge}], scenarios[{id, label, promptTokens, outputTokens}] }` — feed these values into /api/compute.

```bash
# Raw community benchmark runs, filtered + cursor-paginated
curl -s "$BASE/api/localmaxxing?model=qwen3.6-27b&quant=q4_k_m&limit=50"
```
→ `{ snapshot{id, createdAt, runCount}, total, caveats[{code, severity, summary, detail}], items[{runId, modelFamily, hardwareKey, hwClass, engine, quantization, prefillTokPerSec, decodeTokPerSec, contextBand, ageDays, staleness, source}], has_more, next_cursor }` — bare call returns a hardware-group summary instead of items[].

```bash
# Aggregated medians per hardware×model group with bootstrap CIs
curl -s "$BASE/api/benchmarks?groupBy=hardwareModel&limit=25"
```
→ `{ snapshot, total, caveats[], items[{key, runs, prefill{median, q1, q3, min, max, ci95{lo, hi}, label}, decode{…}, engines[], mixedEngines, caveats[], confidence{runs, iqrSpreadPct, outliers, newestRunAgeDays, grade}, crossCheck{relatedRigComparisons, contradictions}, bestRun{runId, …}}], has_more, next_cursor }`.

```bash
# Ranked answer: fastest rigs for ≤8B models at Q4_K_M
curl -s "$BASE/api/best?by=decode&maxParamsB=8&quant=q4_k_m&limit=10"
```
→ `{ id, rankedBy, snapshot, matchedRuns, caveats[], results[{hardware, hardwareKey, hwClass, gpuCount, vramGb, modelFamily, quantization, runsInGroup, confidence{}, medianPrefillTokPerSec, medianDecodeTokPerSec, medianDecodeCi95, medianDecodeLabel, pricing{estimateUsd, lowUsd, highUsd, links{}}, explain}] }` — replayable via `/api/calc/<id>?endpoint=best&<same filters>`.

### Statistical caveats (machine-readable)

`/api/localmaxxing`, `/api/benchmarks` and `/api/best` all return a top-level `caveats` array — objects with `code`, `severity`, `summary`, `detail`. Don't quote benchmark numbers without checking it. Codes:

- `single_stream_only` — dataset only contains batchSize=1 / concurrency≤1 runs; not batched-serving throughput.
- `self_reported_unvalidated` — community-submitted runs, not independently verified; trust medians over single runs.
- `n1_groups` / `n1_group` — some groups (or this row) rest on a single run; treat as anecdotal. Carries `pct`, `groupsWithOneRun`, `totalGroups`.
- `mixed_engines` — a group or the matched set blends different inference engines (llama.cpp vs MLX vs vLLM…).

`/api/best` and `/api/benchmarks` rows also carry a per-row `caveats` array (`n1_group`, `mixed_engines`) when they apply to that specific group.

**GET /api/snapshots** — versioned dataset snapshot IDs (e.g. `snapshot-2026-08-21-a1b2c3d4`). Every data endpoint response carries a `snapshot` object; pass its ID back as `?snapshot=<id>` on `/api/localmaxxing`, `/api/benchmarks` or `/api/best` to pin the dataset and get reproducible numbers. Unknown/expired IDs fall back to current data with `snapshot.served: false`.

Every result includes a `pricing` object: USD street-price estimate (`estimateUsd`, `lowUsd`, `highUsd`), `perGpu` breakdown when gpuCount > 1, an `asOf` date (prices are curated estimates, not live quotes), and `links.ebay` / `links.ebayUsed` / `links.craigslist` search URLs so a budget constraint can be verified against live listings. `pricing` is `null` for cpu_only rigs and unknown GPUs.

### Typical agent workflow

1. `GET /api/sizing?model=<family>&contextLength=…&concurrency=…&maxTpotMs=…` → ranked hardware recommendations with VRAM fit and expected latency, in one call.
1. `GET /api/vram?hfId=<model>&context=<tokens>&vramGb=<budget>` → will it fit, and at what max context? (no model internals needed).
2. `GET /api/best?by=decode&maxParamsB=8` → find the fastest measured hardware for a model class.
3. `GET /api/presets` for canonical speed numbers, or take medians from `/api/benchmarks` for real-world numbers.
4. `GET /api/compute?model=singleTurn&prefillSpeed=...&decodeSpeed=...&promptTokens=...&outputTokens=...` → walltime/TTFT/TPOT for a specific request shape.
5. Compare variants with one call: `POST /api/compute` with `{"batch": [{...}, {...}]}` (up to 50 parameter sets, per-item ok/error status).
6. Citing an answer? Quote the `snapshot.id` from the data response (and re-pin with `?snapshot=<id>`) so the numbers are reproducible later.

All endpoints return JSON, support CORS, need no auth, and set cache headers (10 min on data endpoints).

### Rate limits

Every `/api/*` response carries rate-limit headers so agents can self-throttle:

- `X-RateLimit-Limit` — requests allowed per 60s window per client (currently **120**).
- `X-RateLimit-Remaining` — requests left in the current window.
- `X-RateLimit-Reset` — Unix epoch seconds when the window resets.
- When exhausted, endpoints return **429** with a `Retry-After` header (seconds) and a JSON body explaining the budget. Back off for that many seconds instead of retrying immediately.
- Machine-readable per-operation rate-limit metadata lives in `/api/spec`: every operation carries an `x-rate-limit` object (`enforced`, `limit`, `windowSeconds`, `keying`, `scope`, and for metered endpoints the header names + 429 exhaustion shape). A root-level `x-rate-limit` carries the global default.

Budget: 120 requests/min per client IP. Note this is enforced best-effort **per serverless instance**: Vercel functions share no memory across invocations, so concurrent warm instances each allow 120/min and cold starts reset counters — treat the limit as a floor on good behavior, not a hard global cap.

Every JSON response body also carries the same numbers as a machine-readable `rate_limit` object (`limit`, `remaining`, `reset`, `window_seconds`, `policy`) for clients that only parse bodies. See CHANGELOG-API.md and api/_ratelimit.js for the full contract.

### Schema versioning

Every JSON response carries a top-level `schema_version` field (currently `"1"`) and an `X-Schema-Version: 1` header (also on errors and OPTIONS). Additive changes never bump the version; breaking changes bump the major version and are announced ≥90 days ahead via `Deprecation`, `Sunset`, and `Link; rel="deprecation"` headers. Policy + changelog: /CHANGELOG-API.md in the repo.

Note the two version numbers are independent: `/api/spec`'s `info.version` (currently `2.6.0`) is the API *release* version covering endpoints/params/docs, while wire-level `schema_version` is the response-*contract* version — additive releases bump only `info.version`. The spec mirrors the wire version as `info.x-schema-version`; see CHANGELOG-API.md § "Two version numbers".

### Errors (RFC 9457 problem+json)

Every error response is a single problem object served as `application/problem+json`:

```json
{"type": ".../problems/invalid-params", "title": "Invalid parameters", "status": 400, "detail": "Unknown model 'nope'", "instance": "/api/compute?model=nope", "code": "INVALID_PARAMS"}
```

Branch on the stable `code`, never on `title`/`detail` prose:

| code | HTTP | meaning | retry? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `INVALID_PARAMS` | 400 | bad or missing parameters — fix the input | no (fix first) |
| `NOT_FOUND` | 404 | referenced resource does not exist (reserved) | no |
| `RATE_LIMITED` | 429 | too many requests; honor `Retry-After` | yes, after wait |
| `UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE` | 502 | community-benchmark source temporarily down | yes, with backoff |
| `INTERNAL` | 500 | unexpected server error | maybe |

The machine-readable registry also lives in `/api/spec` (`x-error-codes` + the `Problem` schema) for generated SDKs. Batch items in `/api/compute` carry per-item `code` alongside the human-readable `error` string.

## App tabs (interactive page)

The human-facing UI is this same site. Deep links carry state via URL params: `?tab=<id>`, `preset=<hardware-id>`, `prompt=`, `output=`, `spec=1&draftK=&acc=`. Keyboard: Space play/pause, R reset, Ctrl+Z undo, Ctrl+Shift+Z redo, 1–9 and 0 switch tabs, ? opens the shortcuts dialog.

**Deep-link id vocabularies (authoritative sources):**

- `preset=<hardware-id>` (global): valid ids are the `hardware[].id` enum from **GET /api/presets** (`rtx4090_exl2`, `dual_rtx3090`, `rtx3090_llamacpp`, `mac_ultra`, `rtx3060_entry`, `groq`, `h100`, `rpi5`, `custom`). A value starting with `lmx:` selects a measured LocalMaxxing run.
- On the `kvcache` tab: `gpu=` takes a GPU-catalog id (`rtx5090`, `rtx4090`, `rtx3090`, `rx7900xtx`, `rtx5070ti`, `rtx4060ti16`, `rtx4060`, `rtx6000ada`, `l40s`, `a100`, `h100`, `m4max128`, `m2ultra192`) and `wp=` takes one of `fp16`, `q8`, `q4`.
- **Unknown-id behavior:** an unknown `preset=`, `gpu=` or `wp=` value is never silently swapped for a default and never erased from the URL. The app keeps the original value in the link, shows a visible warning banner, sets `data-invalid-param="<name>=<value>"` on the content root, logs a `console.warn`, and displays default speeds/hardware until you pick a valid id.
Playback speed is deep-linkable on every animated tab: `sim=instant` completes the animation immediately (<1 s; alias `inst` accepted — both spellings work), and numeric multipliers map to the speed buttons as `sim=1|2|5|20`. Combine with `autoplay=1` to start the run on load, e.g. `/?tab=single&autoplay=1&sim=instant` lands on finished output without waiting through real-time animation.

### Instant results on animated tabs (escape hatches)

The single-turn, agentic, batching and A/B tabs animate their simulation (seconds to minutes at 1x). Two supported ways to get the final completed DOM immediately:

- `?sim=instant` — URL-addressable; every animated view jumps straight to the completed state (<1 s). Works on `/` and `/embed` and composes with `autoplay=1` (e.g. `/?tab=agentic&sim=instant&autoplay=1`).
- `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` — the OS-level media query is honored by all four animated views and also forces instant completion. In headless browsers: Playwright context option `reducedMotion: 'reduce'` or CDP `Emulation.setEmulatedMedia({features:[{name:'prefers-reduced-motion', value:'reduce'}]})`. This is environment-based (not shareable via URL), so prefer `?sim=instant` when you control the link.

Both hatches produce the identical final DOM state as a full-speed run; completion is detectable via the view's status text ("Run complete" / phase labels).

<!-- tabs-section:start -->
### Tab: single — Single-turn

- Tab-ID: single
- URL: /?tab=single
- Purpose: Animate one chat request end to end: prompt ingestion (prefill) sets TTFT, then token-by-token generation (decode) sets TPOT and total walltime.
- Surfaces: request timeline animation; speed controls + hardware presets; TTFT/TPOT/walltime metrics; chart + data table; SLO budget checks
- Endpoints: GET /api/compute?model=singleTurn; GET /api/presets

### Tab: agentic — Agentic loop

- Tab-ID: agentic
- URL: /?tab=agentic
- Purpose: Simulate a multi-turn tool-calling loop that re-ingests growing history every turn; compare walltime growth with and without prefix caching.
- Surfaces: turn-by-turn timeline; per-turn token breakdown; prefix-caching toggle; cumulative walltime chart
- Endpoints: GET /api/compute?model=agentic

### Tab: batching — Batching

- Tab-ID: batching
- URL: /?tab=batching
- Purpose: Show concurrent users sharing one accelerator: per-user decode decays as batchSize^(−decodeDecayExponent) with batch size while aggregate throughput climbs — a heuristic power law with NO saturation point, so it must not be used alone to pick an optimal batch size.
- Surfaces: batch-size slider; per-user vs aggregate throughput meters; shared-compute animation
- Endpoints: GET /api/compute?model=batched
- URL params:
  - breqs=<2–48> — concurrent requests in the batch
  - bprompt=<128–32768> — mean prompt tokens per request
  - bgen=<32–4096> — mean output tokens per request
  - bmax=<1–32> — maximum batch size (concurrent decodes)
  - bchunk=<0|128|256|512|1024|2048|4096|8192> — chunked-prefill chunk size; 0 disables chunking. The UI slider is indexed by these stops, so DOM slider position ≠ token value
  - barr=<0–2000, ms> — interval between request arrivals
  - sim=<1|2|5|20|instant> — playback time-scale multiplier shared by all animated tabs

### Tab: compare — Compare

- Tab-ID: compare
- URL: /?tab=compare
- Purpose: Side-by-side hardware comparison at fixed workload shapes, blending built-in presets with measured community benchmark medians.
- Surfaces: hardware preset table; measured-speed columns; apply-measured-speeds action; community run counts
- Endpoints: GET /api/benchmarks; GET /api/best; GET /api/localmaxxing; GET /api/presets

### Tab: ab — A/B

- Tab-ID: ab
- URL: /?tab=ab
- Purpose: Replay two hardware configs head-to-head on the identical workload so prefill/decode differences are visible as a race.
- Surfaces: A/B config pickers; synchronized replay animation; per-phase winner callouts
- Endpoints: GET /api/compute?model=singleTurn

### Tab: diff — Diff

- Tab-ID: diff
- URL: /?tab=diff
- Purpose: Diff two community benchmark runs (or two constraint sets via what-if mode) and read per-metric deltas plus a plain-language summary.
- Surfaces: run A/B free-text id inputs; per-metric delta rows with ratios; plain-language summary; deep links (?tab=diff&runA&runB) auto-execute on load
- Endpoints: GET /api/diff?runA=<id>&runB=<id>; GET /api/diff?mode=whatif

### Tab: shortlist — Find HW

- Tab-ID: shortlist
- URL: /?tab=shortlist
- Purpose: Turn a workload spec into a ranked hardware shortlist: VRAM fit, expected latency vs SLO budgets, and confidence from sample counts.
- Surfaces: workload/constraint form; ranked shortlist table; VRAM fit check; confidence badges
- Endpoints: GET /api/sizing; GET /api/best; GET /api/vram; GET /api/parse-constraints

### Tab: kvcache — KV cache

- Tab-ID: kvcache
- URL: /?tab=kvcache
- Purpose: Compute KV-cache VRAM for a model architecture across context lengths and quantizations, including GQA head layout.
- Surfaces: architecture/model picker; context × precision matrix; quant tradeoff matrix; multi-GPU planner
- Endpoints: GET /api/vram; GET /api/compute?model=kvCache

### Tab: theory — Theory

- Tab-ID: theory
- URL: /?tab=theory
- Purpose: Plain-language guide to why prefill is compute-bound and decode is bandwidth-bound, with analogies, glossary and misconception callouts.
- Surfaces: concept walkthrough; analogies toggle; jargon glossary; misconception callouts
- Endpoints: none (static explainer content)

<!-- tabs-section:end -->

## Embedding (/embed)

`/embed?tab=<id>&…` serves the chrome-less visualizer for cross-origin `<iframe>` embedding. The frame talks back over `window.postMessage`; every message is a `{ type, … }` object:

- Frame → parent: `{ "type": "llmpdv:ready", "tab": "<id>" }` on mount, and `{ "type": "llmpdv:state", "tab": "<id>", "playing": true|false }` whenever the tab or playback state changes.
- Parent → frame: `{ "type": "llmpdv:command", "action": "play" | "pause" | "reset" | "setTab", "tab": "<id>" }` (`tab` required only for `setTab`, ignored otherwise). Commands are accepted only from the direct parent window; anything else is dropped.

There is no dedicated completion event yet — start a run (`autoplay=1` or a `play` command) and watch `llmpdv:state` until `playing` flips back to `false`.

## Trust assumptions (subresource integrity)

No `integrity=` SRI pins ship anywhere today. Same-origin bundles under `/assets/` are content-hash-addressed by filename but not pinned in the HTML, and the Google Fonts CSS plus font binaries load cross-origin from `fonts.googleapis.com` / `fonts.gstatic.com` with no integrity attribute (their responses are UA-dependent, so no stable hash exists — self-host/proxy them if you need verifiable subresources). There is also no Content-Security-Policy header yet. This trust assumption applies to every route, including `/embed`.

Source: https://github.com/riceharvest/llm-prefill-decode-visualizer
